item.title: A reproducible CLI workflow records inputs, commands, versions, parameters, and outputs
item.content: Reproducibility requires more than saving the final result. A workflow should preserve input identity, exact commands/parameters, tool versions, relevant environment/reference versions, and output provenance.
item.explanationMarkdown:
A practical minimum record for a command-line analysis includes:

- exact input files or stable accessions/checksums
- exact command lines and parameters
- program and database/reference versions
- environment information where it affects behavior
- output filenames and a traceable mapping from inputs to outputs

A shell history alone is usually insufficient because it may omit environment state, software versions, input provenance, and failed intermediate attempts.

cards.prompt: What information should you preserve so a command-line bioinformatics analysis can be reproduced later?
cards.answerGuidance: Include exact inputs/provenance, commands and parameters, tool versions, database/reference versions, relevant environment details, and traceable outputs.
